title: Severe alcohol-associated hepatitis
subject: gastroenterology
summary: Diagnose clinically (NIAAA criteria), grade with MELD (above 20 severe) or Maddrey (32 or more), screen for infection, then give prednisolone 40 mg daily for 28 days (plus IV N-acetylcysteine for 5 days) if no contraindication; stop steroids if Lille score at day 7 is above 0.45. Nutrition and abstinence drive survival.

sections.title: Recognise
items: NIAAA probable AH: jaundice onset within 8 weeks in a person drinking more than 40 g/day (women) or 60 g/day (men) for 6 months or more, with less than 60 days of abstinence before jaundice; bilirubin above 3 mg/dL; AST above 50 IU/L with AST/ALT above 1.5, both below 400 IU/L.
Liver biopsy is not needed when criteria are met and there are no confounders; consider it (often transjugular) when the diagnosis is uncertain.
Typical features: jaundice, tender hepatomegaly, fever, leucocytosis, ascites or encephalopathy. SIRS can occur without infection but triples mortality.

Exclude other causes: viral hepatitis (A, B, E), drug-induced injury, autoimmune hepatitis, biliary obstruction, Budd-Chiari syndrome, portal vein thrombosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (ultrasound with Doppler).

sections.title: Severity and pre-steroid screen
items: MELD above 20 = severe AH (ACG 2024): admit, consider corticosteroids. MELD 20 or less = moderate AH.
Maddrey discriminant function = 4.6 x (patient prothrombin time minus control, seconds) + bilirubin (mg/dL). A value of 32 or more = severe, with 30-day mortality of about 20 to 50%.
Steroid benefit is greatest at MELD 21 to 39, limited at 40 to 50 and absent above 50.

Before steroids: blood and urine cultures, chest X-ray, diagnostic paracentesis if ascites; HBsAg (and HBV DNA if positive), HIV, and assessment for tuberculosis; glucose, creatinine and signs of GI bleeding.

sections.title: Supportive care (all patients)
items: Assess alcohol withdrawal with CIWA-Ar and treat symptom-triggered; use benzodiazepines cautiously (short or intermediate-acting such as lorazepam or oxazepam are safer with poor liver function) and distinguish withdrawal from hepatic encephalopathy.
Give thiamine before glucose-containing fluids; replace vitamin B12 and zinc if deficient.

Nutrition: 35 kcal/kg/day with protein 1.2 to 1.5 g/kg/day. Add oral supplements, then nasogastric feeding if intake stays inadequate (intake below 21 kcal/kg/day predicts death). Varices without recent banding or bleeding do not contraindicate an NG tube.
No universal prophylactic antibiotics (ACG 2024); treat proven infection promptly and reassess daily.
Avoid nephrotoxins and NSAIDs; manage AKI, ascites, variceal bleeding and encephalopathy per the specific protocols.

sections.title: Corticosteroids and adjuncts (severe AH)
items: Severe AH (MELD above 20 or Maddrey 32 or more) without contraindications: prednisolone 40 mg orally once daily for 28 days; IV methylprednisolone 32 mg daily if unable to take oral drugs. No evidence favours a particular taper.

Contraindications until controlled: active infection, untreated HBV, uncontrolled diabetes, active GI bleeding, severe renal failure. Steroids can be started once infection, bleeding or AKI is controlled.
Add IV N-acetylcysteine for 5 days to prednisolone (ACG 2024 strong recommendation; AASLD 2019: may improve 30-day survival).
Do not use pentoxifylline (ACG 2024 recommends against). G-CSF and microbiome therapies are not routinely recommended.

sections.title: Response and monitoring
items: Calculate the Lille score on day 7 (day 4 is similarly accurate). Above 0.45 = non-response: stop corticosteroids.
Daily: temperature and infection surveillance (including fungal infection), capillary glucose for steroid-induced hyperglycaemia, creatinine and urine output, bilirubin trend and mental state.
Bilirubin falling to below 0.8 times the admission value by day 7 indicates a good trajectory.

sections.title: Non-responders
items: Steroid non-responders with high risk of death: consider early liver transplantation in highly selected patients according to regional and institutional protocols, or clinical trials.
Non-responders who are not transplant candidates and have 4 or more organ failures: palliative care is appropriate.

sections.title: Abstinence and long-term care
items: Sustained abstinence is the strongest determinant of long-term survival. Offer brief intervention and refer to integrated addiction care before discharge.

Relapse-prevention drugs in liver disease: baclofen (preferred), acamprosate (dose-adjust if creatinine clearance 30 to 50 mL/min, avoid below 30), naltrexone only in compensated disease; avoid disulfiram.
Vaccinate against hepatitis A and B, influenza and pneumococcus; refer decompensated patients for transplant assessment.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Starting steroids without an infection screen, or in untreated HBV.
Continuing steroids for 28 days in Lille non-responders, which adds infection risk without benefit.
Neglecting nutrition or missing Wernicke encephalopathy.
Treating withdrawal with repeated long-acting benzodiazepines and precipitating hepatic encephalopathy.

drugs.name: Prednisolone
drugs.dose: 40 mg orally once daily for 28 days
drugs.notes: Stop at day 7 if Lille score above 0.45. Monitor glucose and infection.

drugs.name: Methylprednisolone
drugs.notes: If oral prednisolone cannot be taken.

drugs.name: N-acetylcysteine (IV, with prednisolone)
drugs.dose: Day 1: 150 mg/kg in 250 mL 5% dextrose over 30 minutes, then 50 mg/kg in 500 mL over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg in 1,000 mL over 16 hours. Days 2 to 5: 100 mg/kg/day
drugs.notes: 5-day regimen used in the trial of prednisolone plus NAC (Nguyen-Khac 2011).

drugs.name: Thiamine
drugs.dose: 100 mg IV or orally daily, given before glucose
drugs.notes: Higher treatment doses if Wernicke encephalopathy is suspected.

drugs.name: Baclofen (alcohol use disorder)
drugs.dose: 5 mg orally three times daily, increased every 3 to 5 days to a maximum of 15 mg three times daily
drugs.notes: Most studied relapse-prevention drug in advanced liver disease; monitor for sedation.
